t: Borobudur was built as one great stupa in the form of a mandala, its stairways and corridors leading pilgrims upward past 1,460 narrative reliefs to 72 Buddhas in perforated stupas.
Abandoned at a date nobody knows and buried under volcanic ash and jungle, but never forgotten locally, it was cleared in 1814 for Stamford Raffles, who brought it to the world's attention.
The restoration of 1975–1982 by Indonesia and UNESCO took down and reset over one million stones, and the temple is again a place of pilgrimage at Vesak.
dyk: In 1896 King Chulalongkorn of Siam was allowed to take home eight cartloads of sculptures from Borobudur; several of them, among them lions and a guardian statue, are now in the National Museum in Bangkok.
ev: Building begins under the Sailendra dynasty, the first of five stages in Jacques Dumarçay's dating
The Sanjaya complete the fifth and last stage of the temple
Mpu Prapanca's Nagarakretagama mentions "the vihara in Budur"
Hermann Cornelius and 200 men clear the monument for Stamford Raffles, who brings it to the world's attention
Jan Willem IJzerman finds that the temple base encloses a hidden foot carved with reliefs
Theodoor van Erp begins the first major restoration, completed in 1911
Indonesia and UNESCO begin the restoration that takes down and resets over one million stones
UNESCO lists the Borobudur Temple Compounds as a World Heritage Site

f.made: Begun under the Sailendra dynasty about 780 and completed under the Sanjaya about 833, in Jacques Dumarçay's dating; no record of its building survives, and its architect, Gunadharma, is named only in Javanese folk tales
f.form: A single great stupa of grey andesite on a natural hill, laid out as a mandala: nine stacked platforms, six square and three circular, rising to a central dome 35 m above the ground, with 2,672 relief panels and originally 504 Buddha statues
f.where: Magelang Regency, near Muntilan, northwest of Yogyakarta, Central Java, Indonesia; sculptures and Buddha heads taken from it are in the Bangkok National Museum, the Tropenmuseum, the Musée Guimet and the British Museum
f.known: the largest Buddhist temple in the world; 1,460 narrative relief panels; 72 Buddhas seated in perforated stupas; the hidden foot with the Karmavibhanga reliefs; the relief of the Borobudur Ship; the Vesak walk from Mendut and Pawon
